result.strongest_objection: The document asserts that `s["beta"]` and `s["gamma"]` are read via strict dictionary access on lines 129 and 134 of `tools/glow_eps_sheet.gd`, and that `sim/protocol.ail:209` always carries `one_minus_beta`. Additionally, claiming this strict access is 'the fix shape that (a) took' contradicts V1, which shows (a) safely guarding against missing keys with `ship.has()`.
result.catch: Unverified premise regarding strict dictionary access in `tools/glow_eps_sheet.gd` and payload contents at `sim/protocol.ail:209`.
result.proposed_fix: Add a Verification Log entry checking lines 129 and 134 of `tools/glow_eps_sheet.gd` (e.g., `sed -n '129p;134p' tools/glow_eps_sheet.gd`) and verifying `sim/protocol.ail:209`. Furthermore, update AC16 to use a valid shell command instead of English prose (`every @@ hunk of git diff... starts within lines 70-82`) to parse the Makefile diff.

result.strongest_objection: The load-bearing L2e1 premise — V11/V12's measured claim that deleting the `holds` clause lets the hintless unlock pass, which is the sole justification for keeping the clause and adding `checkHintless` — was measured only on `ailang` v0.54.5 from `PATH`, not the v0.52.0 binary pinned in CI, and the bridging assertion that `codexReport` uses only `std/json`, `std/string` and `std/list` 'which hold no known version caveat' appears in no verification-log row. The acceptance suite then fails to close the gap it exists to close: AC11's second command pins `$A=runtime/bin/ailang`, but AC11's first command (`make session-audit-test codex-unlocks`) and the entire AC12 mutation drill invoke `make session-audit-test` with no AILANG pin, so the kill-proof — the whole point of L2e1 — can execute on the PATH binary and pass without v0.52.0 ever having been shown to exhibit the FAIL/PASS flip. The risk section resolves this by 'the executor re-runs AC11 and AC12 on runtime/bin/ailang', i.e. by intent rather than by any command in the doc; that is an unverified premise under gate 1, and it underpins one of the three code changes.
result.catch: Two secondary flags: (1) AC12's guard `! grep -q 'holds(h, c1)'` can never succeed in the final state, because L2e1 step 2 adds a comment to `sim/tools/session_audit.ail` whose text contains the literal string `holds(h, c1)` — the deletion assertion is vacuous, the exact check-vacuity class V18 was added to eliminate (the drill's verdict still rides on `test $rc != 0`, so nothing proves the sed actually removed the clause). (2) The premises `s["beta"]`/`s["gamma"]` at `tools/glow_eps_sheet.gd:129`/`134` and the always-emitted `one_minus_beta` at `sim/protocol.ail:209` are line-cited but appear in no verification-log row, unlike every other load-bearing claim in the doc.
result.proposed_fix: Three edits. (1) Add a controller verification row V19: after `make runtime`, re-run the V11 and V12 probes on `runtime/bin/ailang` (v0.52.0) and record identical results (deletion mutant leaves auditPure at session-audit-ok pre-merge; hintless case FAIL with the clause, PASS without), plus the output of an import scan of `sim/tools/session_audit.ail` substantiating the std/json, std/string, std/list claim, plus `grep -n AILANG Makefile mk/m45.mk` proving the make variable the risk section tells the executor to set actually exists and is honored. (2) Pin the interpreter inside the ACs themselves: AC11's first command and AC12 become `make session-audit-test AILANG=runtime/bin/ailang ...` (or the repo's canonical pin), so the acceptance suite cannot pass on the PATH binary. (3) Replace AC12's guard with a fragment unique to the clause, e.g. `! grep -q 'all(\\h\. holds(h, c1), hs)'`, which the added comment cannot match, so the deletion is actually proven.
